Author: Ali Can

> This mini project aims to compare the distribution of random exponential numbers against sample means of random exponential numbers and display the latter is approximately normal.

# 0. Import

``` {r}
suppressPackageStartupMessages({
  library(tidyverse)
  library(e1071)
  library(car)
})
```

# 1. Distribution of Random Exponential Numbers

> Code below will randomly create 1 sample (40 observations) of exponential numbers, take their mean and variance, compare them with the theoretical parameters and graph their sample distribution.

```{r}
set.seed(42)

rate=0.2
n <- 40

nums <- rexp(n, rate=rate)
mean_nums <- mean(nums)
mean_theoretical <- 1/rate
cat("Mean of random exponential numbers:", mean_nums, "\n")
cat("Theoretical mean:", mean_theoretical, "\n")

var_nums <- var(nums)
var_theoretical <- 1/rate^2
cat("Variance of random exponential numbers:", var_nums, "\n")
cat("Theoretical variance:", var_theoretical)

as.data.frame(nums) |>
  ggplot(aes(x=nums)) +
  geom_boxplot(fill="blue", outlier.shape=22) +
  theme_grey() +
  labs(title="The Distribution of Exponential Random Numbers (1 sample, 40 observations)", x="")
```

# 2. Distribution of Sample Means of Random Exponential Numbers

> Code below will randomly create 1000 samples (40 observations each) of exponential numbers, take sample means, take mean of sample means and graph "mean of sample means" distribution.

``` {r}
sample_size <- 1000

means <- apply(matrix(rexp(n=n*sample_size, rate=rate), sample_size), 1, mean)
mean_means <- mean(means)
cat("Mean of sample means of random exponential numbers:", mean_means, "\n")
cat("Theoretical mean:", mean_theoretical, "\n")

var_means <- var(means)
var_theoretical <- 1/rate^2/n
cat("Variance of random exponential numbers:", var_means, "\n")
cat("Theoretical variance:", var_theoretical)

as.data.frame(means) |>
  ggplot(aes(x=means)) +
  geom_histogram(bins=25, fill="orange", color="blue") +
  labs(title="Sample Means Distribution", x="", y="Count") +
  theme_minimal()
```

> We have two results to declare:

> 1. Means of random exponential numbers and sample means of random exponential numbers are quite similar.

> 2. While the distribution of random exponential numbers is an exponential distribution as expected, the distribution of sample means of random exponential numbers is gaussian alike.

# 3. Normality Approximation of Sample Means Distribution

1. Skewness

> Code below will determine skewwness of the distribution of sample means

``` {r}
skew <- skewness(means)
cat("Skewness is: ", skew, "\n")

if(abs(skew)>0.5){
  cat("Considerable skewness!, Normality approximation is low.")
} else{
  cat("Slight skewness!, Normality approximation is high.")
}
```
2. Kurtosis

> Code below will determine kurtosis of the distribution of sample means

``` {r}
kurt <- kurtosis(means)
cat("Kurtosis is: ", kurt, "\n")

if(abs(skew)>1){
  cat("Considerable kurtosis!, Normality approximation is low.")
} else{
  cat("Slight kurtosis!, Normality approximation is high.")
}
```

3. QQ Plot

> Code below will make a comparison between quantiles of the distribution of sample means against standard normal quantiles and graph them.

```{r}
means_scaled <- scale(means)

qqnorm(means_scaled) 

qqline(means_scaled, col = "red")
```

> It is obvious that the sample means approximates normality considerably.
